knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact quadratic-majorant characterization of smooth convexity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable, and let \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convex Hilbert-space regime; the converse from a one-sided quadratic model can fail without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The smooth quadratic upper-bound property with constant \(L\) is \[f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac L2\|y-x\|^2\qquad(\forall x,y\in\mathcal H).\] For convex differentiable \(f\), this property is equivalent to \(L\)-Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla f\), and also to convexity of \(Lq-f\), where \(q(x)=\frac12\|x\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth convex function admits, at every base point, a tangent quadratic majorant with curvature L. In the global Hilbert-space convex setting, existence of all these majorants is exactly equivalent to an L-Lipschitz gradient. It is also equivalent to convexity of the complementary quadratic function.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is Fréchet differentiable on all of \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz}\iff(\forall x,y)\ f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac L2\|y-x\|^2\iff Lq-f\text{ is convex}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quadratic majorant at \(x\) is \(q_x(y)=f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac L2\|y-x\|^2\), and the condition is \(f\le q_x\) for every \(x\).
The equivalent Jensen form is \(f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\ge\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)-\frac L2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(L=0\), the global differentiable case reduces to affine functions, but the stated equivalence is parameterized by \(L>0\).
For a convex quadratic with Hessian \(A\), the property holds exactly when \(A\preccurlyeq LI\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Each model is value- and gradient-matching at its base point.
The inequality supplies a uniform upper bound on the first-order Taylor remainder.
boundary_notes: For a nonconvex function, the descent-lemma inequality can hold with a smaller constant than the gradient Lipschitz modulus.
A local model on a proper subset is not automatically a global smoothness certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Smooth Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The reciprocal-\(L\) formulas require \(L>0\). The restricted-set clause asserts only inequalities (2.1.9), (2.1.12), and (2.1.14), not all six equivalences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be dual to \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \(L>0\). Membership \(f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n,\|\cdot\|)\) is equivalent to each of the following conditions holding for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\) and, where present, all \(\alpha\in[0,1]\):
\[
0\le f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\le\frac L2\|x-y\|^2;
\]
\[
f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac1{2L}\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*^2\le f(y);
\]
\[
\frac1L\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*^2\le\langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle;
\]
\[
0\le\langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\le L\|x-y\|^2;
\]
\[
\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)\ge f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)+\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{2L}\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*^2;
\]
\[
0\le\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y)-f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\le\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)L}{2}\|x-y\|^2.
\]
Moreover, if \(f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(Q)\), then the first and fourth inequalities hold for all \(x,y\in Q\), and the sixth holds for all \(x,y\in Q\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global convex L-smoothness is equivalently characterized by each of six Taylor-remainder, cocoercivity, gradient-monotonicity, and interpolation inequalities. On a subset Q, the extract additionally guarantees only the two-sided Taylor bound, the two-sided gradient inner-product bound, and the two-sided Jensen-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n,\|\cdot\|)\iff\text{each one of the six universal conditions};\quad f\in\mathcal F_L^{1,1}(Q)\Rightarrow\text{conditions 1, 4, and 6 hold on }Q

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Notation for L-Smooth Function Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both the fixed-parameter class and the class admitting some finite nonnegative smoothness parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $L\ge0$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb E$, let $C_L^{1,1}(D)$ denote the differentiable functions $f$ satisfying $\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*\le L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in D$. When $D=\mathbb E$, write $C_L^{1,1}=C_L^{1,1}(\mathbb E)$. Let $C_1^{1,1}$ denote the class of functions belonging to $C_L^{1,1}$ for some $L\ge0$.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to symmetric, possibly indefinite quadratic functions under an arbitrary finite-dimensional ell-p norm and its dual norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Descent-Lemma Constant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The isotropic quadratic attains equality, so the one-half coefficient is sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\frac L2\|x\|^2\), \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \[f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle=\frac L2\|y-x\|^2.\] Hence the coefficient \(L/2\) cannot be uniformly decreased over functions with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L/2\) is the sharp universal coefficient in the descent-lemma remainder bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality case establishing the optimal universal remainder coefficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-Lemma Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An L-Lipschitz gradient bounds the first-order Taylor remainder above by one half L times the squared displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x,y\in C\), Lipschitz continuity of the gradient yields the quadratic upper estimate \[f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Equivalently, the first-order Taylor remainder satisfies \[f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\leq\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Convexity of \(f\) is not required for this one-sided upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\), and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) for all \(x,y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Euclidean descent lemma on a convex domain.

Curvature-Complement Formulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex differentiable function is L-smooth exactly when its complement in the L-curvature quadratic is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable and \(L>0\). Then \[\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f)\le L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\mapsto\frac L2\|x\|^2-f(x)\text{ is convex}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f)\le L\iff (L/2)\|\cdot\|^2-f\text{ is convex}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable convex function on Euclidean space, Lipschitz gradient, quadratic majorization, and a quadratic Bregman-remainder bound are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following conditions are equivalent: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathbb{R}^n\); for all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2;\] and for all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[0\leq D_f(y,x)\leq\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] The lower bound in the last condition is supplied by convexity; the upper bound is the smooth quadratic model inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Gradient \(L\)-Lipschitzness, the quadratic upper bound, and the two-sided Bregman bound are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional global equivalences for differentiable convex functions.

Then \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz if and only if \[x\longmapsto \frac{L}{2}\|x\|^2-f(x)\] is convex. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral upper curvature bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable. Euclidean norms and the Loewner order on symmetric matrices are used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global twice-continuously-differentiable finite-dimensional Euclidean regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Hessian upper-curvature regime with constant \(L\ge0\) is \[
abla^2f(x)\preccurlyeq LI\qquad( orall x\in\mathbb R^n).\] If \(f\) is convex, then \(0\preccurlyeq
abla^2f(x)\preccurlyeq LI\) for every \(x\), and this condition is equivalent to \(L\)-smoothness in the Euclidean norm. Equivalently, \(\lambda_{\max}(
abla^2f(x))\le L\) for all \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A twice-differentiable function has Hessian upper curvature L when every directional second derivative is at most L times the squared direction norm. For convex functions the Hessian is also positive semidefinite, and the spectral upper bound is exactly equivalent to an L-Lipschitz gradient.
assumptions_latex: For the smoothness equivalence, \(f\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ convex and }L\text{-smooth}\iff(\forall x)\ 0\preccurlyeq\nabla^2f(x)\preccurlyeq LI\iff(\forall x)\ \lambda_{\max}(\nabla^2f(x))\le L.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(x,d\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d^T\nabla^2f(x)d\le L\|d\|_2^2\).
The induced spectral norm satisfies \(\|\nabla^2f(x)\|_2\le L\) when the Hessian is positive semidefinite.
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic \(f(x)=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\), the condition is \(A\preccurlyeq LI\).
When \(L=0\) and \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(f\) is affine.
immediate_consequences_latex: All eigenvalues of the Hessian of a convex \(L\)-smooth function lie in \([0,L]\).
The first-order Taylor remainder is bounded above by \(\frac L2\|y-x\|_2^2\).
boundary_notes: The spectral statement uses the Euclidean norm; other norms require the corresponding induced Hessian norm.
Pointwise twice differentiability without continuity may require a more careful formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Hessian Bounds Fail Without Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of controlling negative curvature in the nonconvex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(M>L\ge0\), the function \(f(x)=- rac{M}{2}\|x\|^2\) satisfies \(
abla^2f=-MI\preceq LI\), but \(\operatorname{Lip}(
abla f)=M>L\). Hence the one-sided inequality \(
abla^2f\preceq LI\) characterizes \(L\)-smoothness only when nonnegative curvature is supplied, for example by convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper Loewner bound alone does not control a nonconvex gradient because arbitrarily large negative curvature remains possible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla^2f\preceq LI
ot\Rightarrow\operatorname{Lip}(
abla f)\le L\) without convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Hessian Bounds Fail Without Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Signed Hessian Criterion for Lipschitz Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable characterization without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex and let \(f\in C^2(C)\). Then \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(C\) if and only if \[\|
abla^2 f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L\quad(x\in C),\] equivalently \[-LI\preceq
abla^2f(x)\preceq LI\quad(x\in C).\] The least admissible constant is \(L_*=\sup_{x\in C}\|
abla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), when this supremum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without convexity, a Lipschitz gradient is characterized by a two-sided signed Hessian bound, and the sharp constant is the supremum Hessian operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f;C)=\sup_{x\in C}\|\nabla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Baillon–Haddad equivalence family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable, and let \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global Hilbert-space convex-gradient regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Baillon–Haddad family is the equivalence between \(L\)-Lipschitz continuity and \(1/L\)-cocoercivity of the gradient: \[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\ge rac1L\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|^2\] for all \(x,y\in\mathcal H\). Under scaling, \(L^{-1}
abla f\) is firmly nonexpansive; for \(L=1\), nonexpansiveness and firm nonexpansiveness coincide for gradients of convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For gradients of convex functions, Lipschitz continuity automatically strengthens to cocoercivity with the reciprocal constant, and the two properties are equivalent. After dividing by L, the gradient is firmly nonexpansive, a property stronger than ordinary nonexpansiveness for general operators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz}\iff\nabla f\text{ is }L^{-1}\text{-cocoercive}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(L^{-1}\nabla f\) is firmly nonexpansive.
\(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and monotone with the sharpened inner-product bound shown above.
For \(L=1\), \(\nabla f\) is nonexpansive if and only if it is firmly nonexpansive.
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)=\frac12\langle Ax,x\rangle\) with \(A\) self-adjoint positive semidefinite, then \(\|A\|\langle A(x-y),x-y\rangle\ge\|A(x-y)\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every smooth convex gradient is monotone.
The forward map \(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\) is averaged for \(0<\gamma<2/L\).
boundary_notes: A general Lipschitz monotone operator need not be cocoercive.
Convexity and gradient structure are essential to the equivalence.

notation.meaning: Cocoercivity constant reciprocal to the gradient Lipschitz constant.

children.title: Gradient Cocoercivity
children.top_down_role: Cocoercive structure of smooth convex gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Is Essential for Cocoercivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothness without convexity is insufficient: a concave quadratic has a Lipschitz but anti-monotone gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=-	frac{L}{2}\|x\|_2^2\), the gradient \(
abla f(x)=-Lx\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, but \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle=-L\|x-y\|_2^2<0\] whenever \(x
eq y\). Hence it is not \( eta\)-cocoercive for any \( eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz but not \(\beta\)-cocoercive for any \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of positive cocoercivity for a smooth nonconvex function.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Reciprocal Smoothness Constant
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reciprocal constant 1/L is optimal, as witnessed by the isotropic quadratic of curvature L.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=	frac{L}{2}\|x\|_2^2\), equality holds in \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle= rac1L\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_2^2\] for every \(x,y\). Therefore no constant larger than \(1/L\) is uniformly valid over all convex functions with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uniform Baillon--Haddad constant \(1/L\) is sharp.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the Baillon–Haddad constant over the smooth convex class.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Cocoercivity Refinement
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex smooth gradient simultaneously controls squared displacement and squared gradient change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\geq rac{\mu L}{\mu+L}\|x-y\|_2^2+ rac1{\mu+L}\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\Delta\nabla f,\Delta x\rangle\geq\frac{\mu L}{\mu+L}\|\Delta x\|_2^2+\frac1{\mu+L}\|\Delta\nabla f\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint displacement and gradient-change bound for strongly convex smooth gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Form of Gradient Cocoercivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each Bregman remainder of a smooth convex function controls half the squared gradient change; its symmetric form is Baillon–Haddad cocoercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[f(x)-f(y)-\langle
abla f(y),x-yangle\geq rac1{2L}\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_2^2.\] Its symmetrized form is the \(1/L\)-cocoercivity inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_f(x,y)\geq\frac1{2L}\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2^2\) for all \(x,y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided strengthened first-order inequality for smooth convex gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient Cocoercivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient of an L-smooth convex function on Euclidean space is 1/L-cocoercive: its directional increase controls the squared change of the gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the gradient satisfies
\[
\langle \nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle
\ge \frac{1}{L}\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2^2.
\]
Thus convexity together with \(L\)-Lipschitz continuity of the gradient strengthens ordinary monotonicity of \(\nabla f\) to \(1/L\)-cocoercivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(1/L\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Baillon–Haddad form matching the cited optimization textbook.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cocoercive gradient operator
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\) be a nonempty subset of a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and let \(f\) be differentiable on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator property of a gradient on a Hilbert-space domain; no convexity is built into the bare definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \( eta>0\), the gradient \(
abla f:D	o\mathcal H\) is \( eta\)-cocoercive if \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\ge eta\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|^2\qquad( orall x,y\in D).\] The largest admissible \( eta\), interpreted as a supremum, is the cocoercivity modulus of the gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient is beta-cocoercive when its change has at least beta times its squared norm as alignment with the displacement. This quantitatively combines monotonicity and Lipschitz control in one inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(( orall x,y\in D)\;\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\ge eta\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\beta\nabla f\) is firmly nonexpansive.
For every \(\gamma\in(0,2\beta)\), \(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\) is \(\gamma/(2\beta)\)-averaged.
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is convex and \(L\)-smooth on the whole Hilbert space, then \(\nabla f\) is \(1/L\)-cocoercive.
A firmly nonexpansive gradient is \(1\)-cocoercive.
immediate_consequences_latex: A cocoercive gradient is monotone.
A \(\beta\)-cocoercive gradient is \(1/\beta\)-Lipschitz unless it is constant, with the same inequality valid in the constant case.
boundary_notes: Monotonicity alone does not imply cocoercivity.
The definition uses a Hilbert inner product and is not transferred verbatim to arbitrary Banach spaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Averaged forward-gradient fixed-point map
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable on a real Hilbert space, assume \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(L>0\), and choose \(0<\gamma<2/L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth convex minimization represented as a fixed-point problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the forward-gradient mapping \[T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma
abla f.\] Since \(
abla f\) is \(1/L\)-cocoercive, \(T_\gamma\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\alpha=\gamma L/2\in(0,1)\). Its fixed-point set is \[\operatorname{Fix}T_\gamma=\{x:
abla f(x)=0\}=\operatorname{Argmin}f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient fixed-point interface replaces smooth convex minimization by finding a fixed point of the forward-gradient map. For steps below two over L, the map is averaged and therefore nonexpansive. Its fixed points are exactly the stationary points, which equal the global minimizers of a differentiable convex function.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) is convex and Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\text{ is }(\gamma L/2)\text{-averaged and }\operatorname{Fix}T_\gamma=\operatorname{Argmin}f.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exists a nonexpansive \(R\) such that \(T_\gamma=(1-\gamma L/2)\operatorname{Id}+(\gamma L/2)R\).
The fixed-point equation \(x=T_\gamma x\) is equivalent to \(\nabla f(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\gamma=1/L\), \(T_\gamma\) is firmly nonexpansive.
At \(\gamma=2/L\), the averagedness parameter reaches \(1\); the open-step regime stated here excludes that boundary.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every fixed point is a global minimizer of \(f\).
The mapping is nonexpansive for every \(0<\gamma<2/L\).
boundary_notes: If \(\operatorname{Argmin}f=\varnothing\), the fixed-point set is empty.
The identity with minimizers uses unconstrained convex differentiable optimization; constrained problems require a projection or proximal operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition. As stated, it presupposes that the argmax defines a selection in Q_2; the supplied assumptions alone do not guarantee existence or uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_2\subseteq\mathbb E_2, let \phi:Q_2\to\mathbb R be differentiable, and let L_2(\phi)>0. The adjoint gradient mapping V:Q_2\to Q_2 is defined, for u\in Q_2, by V(u)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{v\in Q_2}\left\{\langle\nabla\phi(u),v-u\rangle_{\mathbb E_2}-\frac{L_2(\phi)}{2}\|v-u\|_{\mathbb E_2}^2\right\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point u, the adjoint gradient mapping selects a point v in Q2 maximizing the linearized increase of phi minus a quadratic displacement penalty with coefficient L2(phi).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V(u)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{v\in Q_2}\left\{\langle\nabla\phi(u),v-u\rangle_{\mathbb E_2}-\frac12L_2(\phi)\|v-u\|_{\mathbb E_2}^2\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth-convex gradient inequality relative to a minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimizer-relative consequence of convexity and Lipschitz gradient regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $L>0$, let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ be convex and continuously differentiable, and suppose $\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$. If $x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(z)$, then for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$\langle
abla f(x),x-x^*angle\ge rac1L\|
abla f(x)\|^2.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex continuously differentiable function with L-Lipschitz gradient, the gradient's inner product with displacement from any unconstrained minimizer is at least the squared gradient norm divided by L.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and continuously differentiable}

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Points of Gradient-Step Maps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive stepsize, the fixed points of a convex gradient-step map are exactly the global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable and let \(\gamma>0\). For \(T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\),
\[
\operatorname{Fix}T_\gamma=\{x:\nabla f(x)=0\}=\operatorname*{argmin}f.
\]
Thus a point is a fixed point of the gradient map exactly when it globally minimizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f)=\operatorname*{argmin}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate supplied by every positive-stepsize gradient map.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Upper Stepsize for Nonexpansiveness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a one-dimensional quadratic, every stepsize above 2/L makes the gradient map expansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac L2x^2\), where \(L>0\). Then
\[
T_\gamma x=(1-\gamma L)x.
\]
If \(\gamma>2/L\), its Lipschitz constant is \(|1-\gamma L|>1\), so \(T_\gamma\) is expansive. Consequently the upper bound \(2/L\) is sharp.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(T_\gamma)=|1-\gamma L|>1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of gradient-map nonexpansiveness beyond 2/L.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Gradient Maps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every stepsize between zero and 2/L, subtracting the scaled gradient defines a nonexpansive map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(T_\gamma x=x-\gamma\nabla f(x)\). Then, for all \(x,y\in H\),
\[
\|T_\gamma x-T_\gamma y\|^2
\le \|x-y\|^2-\gamma\left(\frac{2}{L}-\gamma\right)
\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|^2
\le \|x-y\|^2.
\]
Consequently, every gradient step with \(\gamma\in[0,2/L]\) is nonexpansive.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(L>0\).
\(f:H\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, differentiable, and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexpansiveness of the forward gradient step over its full admissible stepsize interval.

notation.meaning: identity mapping on the Hilbert space

source_witnesses.locator: 4.5 Averaged Nonexpansive Operators p. 81

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Stepsize Boundary for Averaged Gradient Maps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the endpoint 2/L, a quadratic objective yields minus the identity, which is nonexpansive but not strictly averaged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\mathbb R\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac L2x^2\), where \(L>0\). At \(\gamma=2/L\),
\[
T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f=-\operatorname{Id}.
\]
The map \(-\operatorname{Id}\) is nonexpansive but is not \(\alpha\)-averaged for any \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Hence \(0<\gamma<2/L\) is sharp for strict averagedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\gamma=-\operatorname{Id}\) is not \(\alpha\)-averaged for any \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strict averagedness at the endpoint gamma=2/L.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged Gradient Maps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient step with stepsize strictly below 2/L is averaged, with averaging parameter gamma L/2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha=\gamma L/2\in(0,1)\). There exists a nonexpansive mapping \(R:H\to H\) such that
\[
T_\gamma=(1-\alpha)\operatorname{Id}+\alpha R.
\]
Equivalently, one may take
\[
R=\operatorname{Id}-\frac{2}{L}\nabla f,
\]
which is nonexpansive by gradient cocoercivity. Hence \(T_\gamma\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with the explicit parameter \(\alpha=\gamma L/2\).
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(L>0\).
\(f:H\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, differentiable, and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma\nabla f\) is \(\gamma L/2\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaged-operator representation of a smooth convex gradient step.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.5 Averaged Nonexpansive Operators p. 81

knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercivity–Averagedness Translation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Beta-cocoercivity is equivalent to averagedness of every interior-stepsize forward map with parameter gamma divided by 2 beta.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\to H\), \(\beta>0\), and \(0<\gamma<2\beta\). Then \(A\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive if and only if
\[
T_\gamma=\operatorname{Id}-\gamma A
\]
is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\alpha=\gamma/(2\beta)\). Equivalently,
\[
T_\gamma=(1-\alpha)\operatorname{Id}+\alpha(\operatorname{Id}-2\beta A),
\]
and \(\operatorname{Id}-2\beta A\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive if and only if \(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma A\) is \(\gamma/(2\beta)\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Hilbert-space correspondence between cocoercivity and averaged forward maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercivity Translation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Beta-cocoercivity of an operator is exactly nonexpansiveness of its forward map with stepsize 2 beta.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\[
\langle Ax-Ay,x-y\rangle\ge\beta\|Ax-Ay\|^2
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in H,
\]
and
\[
\|(x-2\beta Ax)-(y-2\beta Ay)\|\le\|x-y\|
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in H.
\]
More generally, cocoercivity implies that \(\operatorname{Id}-\gamma A\) is nonexpansive for every \(\gamma\in[0,2\beta]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive if and only if \(\operatorname{Id}-2\beta A\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Hilbert-space translation between cocoercivity and a nonexpansive reflected forward map.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong convexity with quadratic modulus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and let \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued Hilbert-space definition with curvature measured by the Hilbert norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is convex and, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function is strongly convex with parameter mu when its Jensen inequality contains a uniform quadratic deficit proportional to the squared distance between the endpoints. The parameter depends on the ambient norm and measures uniform lower curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\theta\in[0,1])\;f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(f-\frac\mu2\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex.
If \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \(f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|^2\) for every \(g\in\partial f(x)\).
Under the same closed convex hypotheses, \(\partial f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone.
special_cases_latex: The quadratic \(x\mapsto\frac12\langle Ax,x\rangle+b^Tx+c\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex exactly when \(A\succeq\mu I\).
Strong convexity is uniform convexity with modulus \(t\mapsto\frac\mu2t^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A proper closed strongly convex function has at most one minimizer and, on the whole Hilbert space, has a unique minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong convexity in subgradient and differentiable forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition with parameter \(\hat\sigma>0\), preserving the extract's existential subgradient quantifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(\hat f\) is strongly convex with parameter \(\hat\sigma>0\) if, for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f\), there exists \(g\in\partial\hat f(x)\) such that \[\hat f(y)\ge \hat f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] If \(\hat f\) is differentiable, this is equivalent to \[\hat f(y)\ge \hat f(x)+\langle\nabla\hat f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2\qquad\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is strongly convex with positive parameter sigma-hat when every pair of domain points admits the stated quadratic subgradient lower bound. For a differentiable function, the corresponding gradient inequality is equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f\ \exists g\in\partial\hat f(x):\ \hat f(y)\ge\hat f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\tfrac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2,\text{ with }g=\nabla\hat f(x)\text{ in the differentiable case}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Characterizations of Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded equivalence of strong convexity, the global quadratic subgradient inequality, and strong monotonicity of the full subdifferential for a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,\infty] be proper, closed, and convex, and let \sigma>0. The following are equivalent: (i) f is \sigma-strongly convex; (ii) for every x\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial f), every y\in\operatorname{dom}f, and every g\in\partial f(x), \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2;\] (iii) for every x,y\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial f), every g_x\in\partial f(x), and every g_y\in\partial f(y), \[\langle g_x-g_y,x-y\rangle\geq\sigma\lVert x-y\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function and a positive modulus, strong convexity is equivalent to a global quadratic subgradient lower bound and to strong monotonicity of the subdifferential. Both inequalities hold for every point and subgradient in the stated domains.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&f\text{ is }\sigma\text{-strongly convex}\\ &\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall x\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial f),\ \forall y\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \forall g\in\partial f(x),\quad f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\\ &\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial f),\ \forall g_x\in\partial f(x),\ \forall g_y\in\partial f(y),\quad \langle g_x-g_y,x-y\rangle\geq\sigma\lVert x-y\rVert^2.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity of Quadratic Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization and maximal strong-convexity modulus for finite-dimensional quadratics under the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb R^n\) be endowed with the \(\ell_2\)-norm and let
\[
f(x)=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c,
\qquad A\in\mathbb S^n,\quad b\in\mathbb R^n,\quad c\in\mathbb R.
\]
For \(\sigma>0\), \(f\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex if and only if
\[
A-\sigma I\succeq0,
\]
equivalently, if and only if \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq\sigma\). Consequently, \(f\) is strongly convex if and only if \(A\succ0\); when this holds, its largest possible strong-convexity parameter is \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic with symmetric matrix A is sigma-strongly convex exactly when A minus sigma times the identity is positive semidefinite, equivalently when the smallest eigenvalue of A is at least sigma. It is strongly convex exactly when A is positive definite, and then its largest admissible parameter is the smallest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is }\sigma\text{-strongly convex}\iff A-\sigma I\succeq0\iff\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq\sigma;\quad f\text{ is strongly convex}\iff A\succ0,\quad \sigma_{\max}=\lambda_{\min}(A).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Quadratic Supporting Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity is equivalently ordinary convexity after subtracting a quadratic, or a quadratic strengthening of every subgradient supporting model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\mu>0\). Then \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \(x\mapsto f(x)-\frac\mu2\|x\|_2^2\) is convex. Equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), every \(g\in\partial f(x)\), and every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|_2^2.\]
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\frac\mu2\|\cdot\|_2^2\) is convex, equivalently the displayed subgradient lower model holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proper closed convex formulation extending the differentiable seed through quadratic shifting and subgradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Lower-Model Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the differentiable setting, strong convexity means every first-order affine model is strengthened by a quadratic term of curvature mu.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex when, for every \(x,y\in C\),
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2.
\]
Thus every first-order affine model of \(f\) is strengthened by a quadratic term with curvature modulus \(\mu\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty open convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed quadratic lower-model inequality defines \(\mu\)-strong convexity in this differentiable setting.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable quadratic lower-model definition on an open convex Hilbert-space domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Gradient Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable convex function on a Euclidean domain is mu-strongly convex exactly when its gradient is mu-strongly monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic lower-model inequalities
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in C
\]
hold if and only if
\[
\langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_2^2
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in C.
\]
Thus the gradient operator characterizes the same strong-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \(\nabla f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable finite-dimensional characterization matching the cited optimization textbook.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong monotonicity of a gradient
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\) be a convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and let \(f\) be differentiable on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable strong-convexity regime; the definition is stated directly as an operator inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The gradient \(
abla f:D	o\mathcal H\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone, for \(\mu>0\), if \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|^2\qquad( orall x,y\in D).\] For a differentiable convex function on an open convex domain, this condition is equivalent to \(\mu\)-strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient is strongly monotone when its change has a uniformly positive component along every displacement. For differentiable convex functions, this operator inequality is exactly the first-order characterization of strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x,y\in D)\;\langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable convex \(f\), \(f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|^2\).
For a proper closed convex function, the set-valued extension is \(\langle g_x-g_y,x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|^2\) for all \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\), \(g_y\in\partial f(y)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) with symmetric \(A\), strong gradient monotonicity is \(A\succeq\mu I\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A \(\mu\)-strongly monotone gradient is injective.
If a zero of the gradient exists, it is unique.
boundary_notes: Ordinary monotonicity corresponds to convexity but does not imply any positive modulus.

children.title: Hessian Lower-Curvature Regimes
children.top_down_role: Twice-differentiable spectral characterizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexity Does Not Imply Uniform Hessian Curvature
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strictly convex function x to the fourth is not strongly convex because its Hessian vanishes at the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f(x)=x^4\) is strictly convex on \(\mathbb R\), but \(f''(0)=0\). Hence there is no \(\mu>0\) such that \(f''(x)\ge\mu\) for all \(x\), so \(f\) is not strongly convex on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is strictly convex but is not \(\mu\)-strongly convex for any \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between strict convexity and a uniform positive Hessian lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Lower-Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function, mu-strong convexity is equivalent to every Hessian eigenvalue being at least mu.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(C\) if and only if, for every \(x\in C\) and \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2 f(x)v\ge\mu\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Equivalently, every eigenvalue of \(\nabla^2f(x)\) is at least \(\mu\), or \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\), throughout \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional twice-continuously-differentiable spectral characterization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral lower curvature bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, let \(f\in C^2(D)\), and let \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-continuously-differentiable finite-dimensional Euclidean characterization of strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Hessian lower-curvature regime with parameter \(\mu\) is \[
abla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\qquad( orall x\in D).\] Equivalently, \(d^T
abla^2f(x)d\ge\mu\|d\|_2^2\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\ge\mu\) for every \(x\). In this regime, \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(D\), and conversely every \(C^2\) \(\mu\)-strongly convex function satisfies the Hessian bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A twice-differentiable function has lower curvature mu when every Hessian eigenvalue is at least mu throughout its convex domain. This spectral condition is equivalent to strong convexity in the Euclidean twice-differentiable setting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex on }D\iff(\forall x\in D)\ \nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\iff(\forall x\in D)\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge\mu.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(f-\frac\mu2\|\cdot\|_2^2\) has positive semidefinite Hessian everywhere and is convex.
Every directional second derivative satisfies \(D^2f(x)[d,d]\ge\mu\|d\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic with Hessian \(A\), the largest strong-convexity parameter is \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\).
Taking \(\mu=0\) recovers the Hessian criterion for ordinary convexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Hessian is positive definite at every point when \(\mu>0\).
The gradient is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness at each point without a uniform eigenvalue lower bound need not yield global strong convexity with a positive constant.
The matrix inequality is tied to the Euclidean norm.

children.title: Strong Convexity–Conjugate Smoothness Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Dual exchange between lower curvature and differentiable smoothness.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Gradient as Unique Primal Maximizer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient of the conjugate of a strongly convex function is the unique primal maximizer and inverts the primal subdifferential relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), then for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\) the supremum defining \(f^*(u)\) has a unique maximizer and \[\nabla f^*(u)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}.\] Equivalently, \(u\in\partial f(x)\) if and only if \(x=\nabla f^*(u)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f^*(u)=\operatorname*{argmax}_x\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\},\quad u\in\partial f(x)\iff x=\nabla f^*(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimizer representation induced by strong convexity in the conjugate correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity–Conjugate Smoothness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex f is mu-strongly convex exactly when its conjugate is differentiable with a 1/mu-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if its Fenchel conjugate
\[
f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}
\]
is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) and satisfies
\[
\|\nabla f^*(u)-\nabla f^*(v)\|_2\le\frac{1}{\mu}\|u-v\|_2
\quad\text{for all }u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The reciprocal constant \(1/\mu\) is the conjugate smoothness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \(f^*\) is differentiable with \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Fenchel-conjugacy correspondence with reciprocal moduli.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel-conjugate curvature correspondence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathbb E\) be a finite-dimensional normed space with dual \(\mathbb E^*\), let \(\mu>0\), and define \(f^*(u)=\sup_x\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Fenchel conjugacy with primal and dual norms; closedness is required in the strong-convexity-to-smoothness direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The strong-convexity–conjugate-smoothness correspondence is: if \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, then \(f^*:\mathbb E^*\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable everywhere and \(\nabla f^*\) is \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz from the dual norm to the primal norm. Conversely, if \(g:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) is convex and \(1/\mu\)-smooth, then \(g^*\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to the dual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugacy exchanges uniform quadratic lower curvature with an upper Lipschitz-gradient bound. A proper closed mu-strongly convex function has an everywhere finite conjugate whose gradient is Lipschitz with reciprocal constant. Conversely, a finite smooth convex function has a strongly convex conjugate.
assumptions_latex: For the forward direction, \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
For the converse direction, \(g\) is finite, convex, and \(1/\mu\)-smooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ proper closed and }\mu\text{-strongly convex}\Rightarrow f^*\text{ is }\mu^{-1}\text{-smooth};\quad g\text{ convex and }\mu^{-1}\text{-smooth}\Rightarrow g^*\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the forward direction, \(\nabla f^*=(\partial f)^{-1}\) is single-valued and \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz.
For closed proper convex \(f\), applying both directions to \(f\) and \(f^*\) yields the biconditional with the appropriate primal and dual norms.
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\frac12x^TAx\) with \(A\succ0\), \(f^*(u)=\frac12u^TA^{-1}u\); the lower eigenvalue bound for \(A\) becomes an upper eigenvalue bound for \(A^{-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Strong convexity ensures uniqueness of the maximizer defining \(f^*(u)\) for every \(u\).
The reciprocal relationship exchanges the constants \(\mu\) and \(1/\mu\).
boundary_notes: Without closedness, the forward statement is naturally applied to the closed convex representative.
Smoothness of \(f^*\) does not assert strong convexity of \(f^*\); it corresponds to strong convexity of \(f\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform convexity with a modulus
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and let \(\phi:\mathbb R_+\to[0,+\infty]\) be increasing and vanish only at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued Hilbert-space uniform convexity, including nonquadratic moduli and power-type subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is uniformly convex with modulus \(\phi\) if, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), \[f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)+\theta(1-\theta)\phi(\|x-y\|)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y).\] It is uniformly convex if it admits at least one such modulus. A power-type modulus has the form \(\phi(t)=c t^p\) with \(c>0\) and an admissible exponent \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convexity strengthens strict convexity by requiring a Jensen deficit controlled solely by the distance between the two endpoints. The controlling function is the modulus of convexity and need not be quadratic. Strong convexity is the quadratic special case.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is required for all domain points and all \(0<\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\theta\in(0,1))\;f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)+\theta(1-\theta)\phi(\|x-y\|)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact modulus is the pointwise infimum of the normalized Jensen deficit over pairs at a prescribed distance and mixing parameters.
Uniform convexity holds exactly when the exact modulus vanishes only at \(0\).
special_cases_latex: Strong convexity with constant \(\mu\) corresponds to \(\phi(t)=\frac\mu2t^2\).
Functions such as \(\|\cdot\|^p\) for \(p\ge2\) provide standard nonquadratic uniformly convex examples.
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform convexity implies strict convexity.
If \(f\) is proper and convex, uniform convexity of \(f\) with modulus \(\phi\) makes \(\partial f\) uniformly monotone with modulus \(2\phi\).
boundary_notes: Strict convexity need not be uniform on an unbounded domain.
The modulus and power-type constants depend on the norm and on whether the property is global or restricted to a subset.

children.title: Modulus-Based Uniform Convexity
children.top_down_role: General quantitative curvature controlled by a modulus.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexity Need Not Be Uniform
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential is strictly convex, but its fixed-distance Jensen gaps have no positive location-independent lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f(x)=e^x\) is strictly convex on \(\mathbb R\), but it is not uniformly convex with any modulus positive at every nonzero distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is strictly convex but not uniformly convex in the seed's sense.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why a location-independent positive distance modulus is stronger than strict convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Growth from the Uniform Modulus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Jensen modulus yields a subgradient remainder bound and quantitative monotonicity of the subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) satisfies the seed's uniform-convexity inequality, then for \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(s\in\partial f(x)\),
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|x-y\|).
\]
Consequently, if \(r\in\partial f(y)\), then
\[
\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2\phi(\|x-y\|).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies the accepted seed's uniform-convexity inequality with modulus \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-f(x)-\langle s,y-x\rangle\ge\phi(\|x-y\|)\) and \(\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2\phi(\|x-y\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way consequence under the seed's Jensen-gap normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictness and Uniqueness Consequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive uniform-convexity modulus implies strict convexity and uniqueness of any minimizer over a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A uniformly convex function whose modulus satisfies \(\phi(r)>0\) for \(r>0\) is strictly convex on its effective domain. It therefore has at most one minimizer on each convex subset of that domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies the accepted seed's uniform-convexity inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is strictly convex, and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)\) contains at most one point for every convex \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a minimizer is not asserted.

knowledge_statements.title: Modulus-Based Uniform Convexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convexity requires the Jensen gap to dominate a positive modulus depending on the distance between the two points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is uniformly convex with modulus \(\phi\) when, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(t\in[0,1]\),
\[
f((1-t)x+ty)
\le (1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-t(1-t)\phi(\|x-y\|).
\]
Positivity of \(\phi(r)\) for every \(r>0\) makes the convexity inequality quantitatively strict at every nonzero separation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a normed space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Jensen gap condition defines uniform convexity with modulus \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jensen-gap convention with an explicit distance modulus.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Uniform and Strong Convexity p. 178

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient Growth Induced by the Uniform Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-way consequence of the seed's Jensen-gap normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) satisfies
\[
f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-t(1-t)\phi(\|x-y\|),
\]
then for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(s\in\partial f(x)\),
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|x-y\|).
\]
Hence, for \(s\in\partial f(x)\) and \(r\in\partial f(y)\),
\[
\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2\phi(\|x-y\|).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Jensen modulus yields a matching subgradient remainder and quantitative monotonicity of the subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies the immutable seed's uniform-convexity inequality with modulus \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-f(x)-\langle s,y-x\rangle\ge\phi(\|x-y\|)\) and \(\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2\phi(\|x-y\|)\).

children.title: Power-Type Uniform Convexity
children.top_down_role: Polynomial curvature regimes extending strong convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Power Classes Are Distinct
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the whole real line, quadratic strong convexity is not power-type uniform convexity with an exponent other than two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), a global deficit \(c\,t(1-t)|x-y|^p\) with \(c>0\) exists exactly when \(p=2\). It fails for \(1<p<2\) at arbitrarily small separations and for \(p>2\) at arbitrarily large separations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits a global positive power-type constant with exponent \(p\) if and only if \(p=2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that different power exponents are not interchangeable on an unbounded domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Power Growth of Subgradients and Objective Error
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-type uniform convexity yields p-order subgradient growth and a p-order objective-error bound around a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is uniformly convex of power type \(p\) with constant \(c\), then
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+c\|y-x\|^p
\quad(s\in\partial f(x)),
\]
and
\[
\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2c\|x-y\|^p
\quad(s\in\partial f(x),\ r\in\partial f(y)).
\]
Every global minimizer \(x_*\) satisfies
\[
f(x)-f(x_*)\ge c\|x-x_*\|^p.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies the accepted seed with \(\phi(r)=cr^p\), where \(c>0\) and \(p>1\).
The displayed subgradients exist at the relevant points.
\(x_*\) is a global minimizer when the objective-error assertion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2c\|x-y\|^p\), and \(f(x)-f(x_*)\ge c\|x-x_*\|^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constants use the accepted seed's Jensen-gap normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Type Uniform Convexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-type uniform convexity uses a Jensen-gap modulus equal to a positive constant times the p-th power of distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is uniformly convex of power type \(p\) with constant \(c\) when, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(t\in[0,1]\),
\[
f((1-t)x+ty)
\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-c\,t(1-t)\|x-y\|^p.
\]
This is modulus-based uniform convexity with \(\phi(r)=cr^p\). The case \(p=2\) recovers quadratic uniform curvature up to the chosen normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a normed space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is uniformly convex of power type \(p\) with constant \(c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-modulus specialization of uniform convexity.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Uniform and Strong Convexity p. 178

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Curvature Does Not Change Power Globally
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that different power classes are genuinely distinct on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), the Jensen gap is \(\tfrac12t(1-t)|x-y|^2\). Therefore an inequality with deficit \(c\,t(1-t)|x-y|^p\) for all \(x,y\) and some \(c>0\) can hold only for \(p=2\): for \(1<p<2\) it fails as \(|x-y|\to0\), and for \(p>2\) it fails as \(|x-y|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the whole real line, quadratic strong convexity is not power-type uniform convexity with any exponent other than two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits a global positive power-type constant with exponent \(p\) if and only if \(p=2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Curvature Does Not Change Power Globally

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Power Function Induced by a Euclidean Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a centered norm-power function in a positive-definite Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix $x_0\in\mathbb{E}$, and let $B$ be positive definite with induced Euclidean norm
\[
\|h\|=\langle Bh,h\rangle^{1/2}.
\]
The power function of degree $p$ centered at $x_0$ is
\[
d_p(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x-x_0\|^p,\qquad x\in\mathbb{E}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a center x_0 and the Euclidean norm induced by a positive-definite operator B, the power function of degree p is one over p times the pth power of the distance from x to x_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb{E},\quad d_p(x)=\frac1p\|x-x_0\|^p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Difference Upper Bound for the Bregman Remainder
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An upper bound on an oriented first-order remainder under power-type uniform convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{E}$ be convex, let $p\ge 2$, and let $d:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable and uniformly convex on $Q$ of degree $p$ with parameter $\sigma_p>0$. Then, for every $x,y\in Q$,
\[
d(y)-d(x)-\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle
\le \frac{p-1}{p}\,\sigma_p^{-1/(p-1)}\|\nabla d(y)-\nabla d(x)\|_*^{p/(p-1)}.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient Uniform Monotonicity Implies Power-Type Uniform Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for power-type uniform convexity of a differentiable function on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q$ be closed and convex and let $d:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. Suppose that for some $p\ge 2$ and $\sigma>0$,
\[
\langle\nabla d(x)-\nabla d(y),x-y\rangle\ge \sigma\|x-y\|^p,\qquad \forall x,y\in Q.
\]
Then $d$ is uniformly convex on $Q$ of degree $p$ with parameter $\sigma$; that is,
\[
d(y)\ge d(x)+\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{p}\|y-x\|^p,\qquad \forall x,y\in Q.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the gradient of a differentiable function on a closed convex set is uniformly monotone with p-power modulus sigma, then the function is uniformly convex of degree p with the same parameter sigma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,y\in Q,\quad d(y)\ge d(x)+\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{p}\|y-x\|^p

Let $p\ge2$ and let $d_p(x)=p^{-1}\|x-x_0\|^p$ be the power function on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}$. Then, for every $x,y\in\mathbb{E}$,

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient of a Centered Euclidean Norm-Power Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability and the gradient formula for a centered power of a Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $\mathbb{E}$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space equipped with a Euclidean inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and associated norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $B:\mathbb{E}\to\mathbb{E}$ satisfy
\[
\langle u,v\rangle=\langle Bu,v\rangle_{\mathrm{can}},\qquad \forall u,v\in\mathbb{E}.
\]
Fix $x_0\in\mathbb{E}$ and $p\ge2$, and define
\[
d_p(x)=\frac1p\|x-x_0\|^p.
\]
Then $d_p$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{E}$ and
\[
\nabla d_p(x)=\|x-x_0\|^{p-2}B(x-x_0),\qquad \forall x\in\mathbb{E}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the centered norm-power function is differentiable for p at least two, and its gradient is the displacement transformed by the metric operator B and scaled by the displacement norm to the power p−2.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb{E}\text{ is a finite-dimensional real vector space}
\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\text{ is a Euclidean inner product with associated norm }\|\cdot\|
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_p\text{ is differentiable on }\mathbb{E}\quad\text{and}\quad\forall x\in\mathbb{E},\ \nabla d_p(x)=\|x-x_0\|^{p-2}B(x-x_0)

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Convexity–Dual Smoothness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform curvature controlled by phi corresponds under Fenchel conjugacy to dual smoothness controlled by the scalar conjugate phi-star.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The curvature condition
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|y-x\|)
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in X\text{ and }s\in\partial f(x)
\]
is equivalent, under the stated hypotheses, to differentiability of \(f^*\) on \(X^*\) together with
\[
f^*(v)\le f^*(u)+\langle\nabla f^*(u),v-u\rangle
+\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*)
\quad\text{for all }u,v\in X^*.
\]
Thus primal curvature and dual smoothness exchange conjugate moduli.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space with dual \(X^*\).
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\phi\) is proper, convex, nondecreasing, supercoercive, and satisfies \(\phi(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(\phi\)-curvature inequality for \(f\) is equivalent to the \(\phi^*\)-smoothness inequality for \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional subgradient formulation using Fenchel-conjugate moduli.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the function and scalar modulus

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied for the exact bidirectional theorem. The differentiability conclusion, global domains, and use of the scalar conjugate modulus depend on conventions and hypotheses that require authoritative source confirmation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modulus-paired uniform convexity and dual smoothness
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a real Banach space with dual \(X^*\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in X}\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}\). Let \(\phi:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) be convex with \(\phi(0)=0\), and define \(\phi^*(s)=\sup_{t\geq0}\{st-\phi(t)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition records a norm-dependent Banach-space correspondence using first-order remainder inequalities. It does not assert that every modulus yields the displayed dual relation without additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((f,f^*)\) has the uniform-convexity–dual-smoothness correspondence with primal modulus \(\phi\) when, for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) and every \(u\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle u,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|y-x\|),\] and, dually, for every \(u,v\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f^*\) and every \(x\in\partial f^*(u)\), \[f^*(v)\leq f^*(u)+\langle v-u,x\rangle+\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*).\] The first inequality defines uniform convexity through a subgradient remainder; the second defines the matched uniform smoothness of the conjugate through the scalar conjugate modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function and its Fenchel conjugate form a modulus-paired uniformly convex and dually smooth pair when every primal subgradient model underestimates the function by at least \(\phi(\|y-x\|)\), while every dual subgradient model overestimates the conjugate by at most \(\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*)\). The norm and dual norm are part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(y)-f(x)-\langle u,y-x\rangle\geq\phi(\|y-x\|),\qquad f^*(v)-f^*(u)-\langle v-u,x\rangle\leq\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the Bregman remainder \(D_f^u(y,x)=f(y)-f(x)-\langle u,y-x\rangle\), the primal condition is \(D_f^u(y,x)\geq\phi(\|y-x\|)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\phi(t)=\frac{\mu}{2}t^2\), the primal condition is \(\mu\)-strong convexity; its classical dual counterpart is differentiability of \(f^*\) with \((1/\mu)\)-Lipschitz gradient under the usual closedness and full-domain hypotheses.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\phi(t)>0\) for every \(t>0\), the primal inequality implies strict convexity on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
boundary_notes: The numerical modulus changes with the chosen norm.
The displayed generalized dual modulus requires an exact supporting source; the available source material only separately supports uniform convexity and quadratic strong-convexity duality.

notation.meaning: one-dimensional Fenchel conjugate of the modulus on the nonnegative half-line

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative smoothness and relative strong convexity pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(h:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and put \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\cap Q\). Assume \(h\) and \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are differentiable on \(U\). Define \(D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional differentiable relative curvature on a specified comparison set. Nonsmooth reference geometries require subgradient-based variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants \(0\leq\mu\leq L<+\infty\), the pair \((f,h)\) is \((\mu,L)\)-relatively curved on \(U\) if, for all \(x,y\in U\), \[\mu D_h(y,x)\leq f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\leq L D_h(y,x).\] The upper inequality defines \(L\)-relative smoothness of \(f\) with respect to \(h\), and the lower inequality defines \(\mu\)-relative strong convexity. The ordered data \((f,h,Q,\mu,L)\), rather than \(f\) alone, constitutes the relative curvature class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective-reference pair \((f,h)\) has relative curvature parameters \((\mu,L)\) when the first-order remainder of \(f\) lies between \(\mu\) and \(L\) times the Bregman divergence generated by \(h\), for every ordered pair of points in the declared domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x,y\in U:\quad \mu D_h(y,x)\leq D_f(y,x)\leq L D_h(y,x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(f\) and \(h\) are differentiable convex functions on an open convex set, the condition is equivalent to convexity of \(f-\mu h\) and \(Lh-f\) on that set.

If both functions are twice differentiable, the condition is equivalently \(\mu
abla^2h(x)\preceq
abla^2f(x)\preceq L
abla^2h(x)\) for every \(x\in U\).
special_cases_latex: For \(h(x)=\frac12\|x\|_2^2\), the definition reduces to ordinary \(L\)-smoothness and \(\mu\)-strong convexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\mu>0\) and \(h\) is strictly convex, then \(f\) is strictly convex on \(U\).
boundary_notes: The constants are meaningful only relative to the chosen generator and comparison domain.
Boundary points at which the gradients do not exist are excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Smoothness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative smoothness bounds the first-order remainder of the objective by a multiple of the reference Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(f,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable, and let \(L\ge0\). The function \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth relative to \(h\) when \(Lh-f\) is convex on \(C\). Equivalently, for all \(x,y\in C\), \[D_f(y,x)\le LD_h(y,x),\] or \[f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+LD_h(y,x).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is }L\text{-smooth relative to }h\iff Lh-f\text{ is convex}\iff D_f\le LD_h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable finite-dimensional upper curvature relative to a Bregman reference.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer of Relative Accuracy from a Surrogate Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient smoothing or approximation order converts relative accuracy for a positive surrogate into the same relative accuracy for the target objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta>0\), \(r>1\), and let \(\phi,f_p:Q\to\mathbb{R}_{++}\) satisfy \(\tfrac12\phi(y)^2\le f_p(y)\le \tfrac12 r^{1/p}\phi(y)^2\) for every \(y\in Q\). Define \(f_p^*=\inf_{y\in Q}f_p(y)\) and \(\phi_*=\inf_{y\in Q}\phi(y)\). If \(p\in\mathbb N\) satisfies \(p\ge \frac{1+\delta}{\delta}\ln r\), then every \(\bar y\in Q\) satisfying \(f_p(\bar y)\le(1+\delta)f_p^*\) also satisfies \(\phi(\bar y)\le(1+\delta)\phi_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive objectives related by the stated two-sided multiplicative bound, choosing the approximation order at least ((1+delta)/delta) log r ensures that a (1+delta)-relative solution of the surrogate is also a (1+delta)-relative solution of the target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(\bar y)\le(1+\delta)\phi_*

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Growth at a Stationary Minimizer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity converts Bregman distance from a stationary point into an objective-gap lower bound and yields uniqueness for a strict reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\) and \(x_*\in C\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\), then \[f(y)-f(x_*)\ge\mu D_h(y,x_*)\qquad(y\in C).\] If \(\mu>0\) and \(h\) is strictly convex, then \(x_*\) is the unique minimizer of \(f\) on \(C\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\) on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-f(x_*)\ge\mu D_h(y,x_*)\); if \(\mu>0\) and \(h\) is strictly convex, \(x_*\) is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap certificate and uniqueness consequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Relative Modulus Need Not Imply Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate quadratic reference permits a positive relative modulus while leaving an affine family of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(h(x_1,x_2)=\frac12x_1^2\) and \(f=\mu h\) with \(\mu>0\). Then \(f-\mu h=0\) is convex, so \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\), but \[\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\), but its minimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure under a reference with flat directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity lower-bounds the objective's first-order remainder by a multiple of the reference Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(f,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable, and let \(\mu\ge0\). The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\) when \(f-\mu h\) is convex on \(C\). Equivalently, for all \(x,y\in C\), \[D_f(y,x)\ge\mu D_h(y,x),\] or \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\mu D_h(y,x).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex relative to }h\iff f-\mu h\text{ is convex}\iff D_f\ge\mu D_h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable finite-dimensional lower curvature relative to a Bregman reference.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by a differentiable convex function.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Characterization of Relative Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity is equivalent to pointwise lower domination of the objective Hessian over the reference Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If additionally \(f,h\in C^2(C)\), then \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\) if and only if \[
abla^2f(x)\succeq\mu
abla^2h(x)\qquad(x\in C).\] If \(
abla^2h(x)\succ0\) everywhere, the largest admissible modulus is \[\mu_*=\inf_{x\in C}\lambda_{\min}\!\left(
abla^2h(x)^{-1/2}
abla^2f(x)
abla^2h(x)^{-1/2}ight).\]
assumptions_latex: The generalized-eigenvalue formula additionally assumes \(\nabla^2h(x)\succ0\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex relative to }h\iff\nabla^2f\succeq\mu\nabla^2h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable relative lower-curvature test.

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Growth from a Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-growth and uniqueness consequence under relative strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\) on \(C\), and \(x_*\in\operatorname{int}C\) minimizes \(f\) over \(C\) with \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\). Then \[f(y)-f(x_*)\ge\mu D_h(y,x_*)\qquad(y\in C).\] If \(\mu>0\) and \(h\) is strictly convex, then \(D_h(y,x_*)>0\) for \(y\ne x_*\), so \(x_*\) is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity converts Bregman distance from a stationary minimizer into an objective-gap lower bound and yields uniqueness for a strict reference.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\).
\(x_*\) is an interior minimizer with \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-f(x_*)\ge\mu D_h(y,x_*)\); strict \(h\) and \(\mu>0\) imply uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Growth from a Minimizer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Relative Modulus Does Not Ensure Uniqueness for a Degenerate Reference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of strict reference geometry for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(h(x_1,x_2)=\frac12x_1^2\) and \(f=\mu h\) with \(\mu>0\). Then \(f-\mu h=0\) is convex, so \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\), but \[\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.\] Thus a positive relative modulus does not imply ordinary strict convexity or a unique minimizer when the reference has flat directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate quadratic reference permits positive relative strong convexity while leaving an entire affine set of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\), but its minimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Relative Modulus Does Not Ensure Uniqueness for a Degenerate Reference
